paper.title: A Perturbation Approach to Unconstrained Linear Bandits

unmapped: Action set is all of R^d (unconstrained bandit linear optimization)
Losses satisfy ||l_t|| <= G (G plays the role of the Lipschitz constant, mapped to L_lip in learner_knows)
Both loss sequence and comparator(s) are F_0-measurable (fully oblivious)
Comparator-adaptive guarantees: bound holds uniformly over comparators u in R^d, with risk-control R_T(0) <= eps
settings.definition_quote: In what follows, the oblivious setting refers to fully oblivious settings where both the loss sequence and the comparator sequence are F_0 measurable (e.g., determined before the start of the game).

unmapped: Action set is all of R^d (unconstrained bandit linear optimization)
Comparator (and its norm) may be data-dependent / chosen adaptively, e.g. post hoc
Comparator-adaptive guarantees uniformly over comparators in R^d
settings.definition_quote: In this work we focus in particular on unconstrained bandit linear optimization (uBLO), in which the action set is W=R^d ... the learner observes only the scalar output f_t(w_t)=<l_t,w_t> for some vector l_t with ||l_t|| <= G

settings.name_in_paper: Linear bandits on the unit Euclidean ball, stochastic loss vectors (lower bound)
unmapped: Loss vectors l_t i.i.d. from a sub-Gaussian distribution with mean theta and E||l||^2 <= 1; learner observes <l_t, x_t> (noise inside the inner product)
settings.definition_quote: There exists a parameter theta in R^d and a sub-Gaussian distribution P_theta, such that E[l]=theta, E[||l||^2]<=1

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial linear bandits on the unit Euclidean ball (lower bound)
settings.definition_quote: There exists a sequence of losses l_1,...,l_T satisfying ||l_t||<=1 for all t, a comparator u in B_d

settings.name_in_paper: Unconstrained OCO with dynamic regret (full information)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Full-information online convex optimization subroutine result, not a bandit problem
unmapped: Dynamic regret against arbitrary comparator sequences
settings.definition_quote: we focus on a general OCO setting in which the losses (f_t) are arbitrary L-Lipschitz convex functions.

PABLO with Algorithm 6 (Dynamic Algorithm for Unconstrained OLO)

source.label: thm:expected-static
source.quote: For any u in R^d, PABLO equipped with [Jacobsen & Cutkosky, Algorithm 4] with parameter eps/d guarantees E[R_T(u)] = Õ(G eps + d/kappa E[||u|| sqrt(V_T log_+(d||u||Lambda_T/(G eps)))]), where V_T=sum ||l_t||^2, Lambda_T=G sqrt(T) log^2(1+T), and kappa = sqrt(d) in the oblivious setting and kappa=1 otherwise.

results.notes: Oblivious case kappa=sqrt(d) gives sqrt(d) factor. log_+ written as log(1+...) following appendix. Holds more generally for partially-oblivious settings (Remark 1). Regret defined with realized losses against fixed u; oblivious losses so expectation over learner randomness.

symbols.u_norm: comparator norm ||u|| (may be random/data-dependent; bound is in expectation over it)

conditions: expression is inside an expectation over the (possibly data-dependent) comparator norm and losses

source.label: thm:expected-static
source.quote: ... and kappa = sqrt(d) in the oblivious setting and kappa=1 otherwise.

results.notes: Norm-adaptive case kappa=1; the E[] wraps ||u|| sqrt(V_T ...).

bound.expression: sqrt(d)*sqrt((Phi_T + P_Phi)*W_T) + d*G*(eps_risk + M_cmp + Phi_T + P_Phi)

source.label: thm:expected-dynamic
source.quote: For any sequence u_{1:T} in R^d, PABLO equipped with Algorithm dynamic-meta-olo tuned with eps/d guarantees E[R_T(u_{1:T})] = O(E[d/kappa sqrt((Phi_T+P_T^Phi) sum ||l_t||^2||u_t||) + dG(eps+max_t||u_t||+Phi_T+P_T^Phi)]) where kappa = sqrt(d) in the oblivious setting and kappa=1 otherwise

results.notes: Dynamic regret against arbitrary comparator sequences (no prior knowledge of P_T); comparator field set to best_switching_sequence as closest vocab. Appendix uses 4T^3 inside log of P_Phi.

bound.expression: d*sqrt((Phi_T + P_Phi)*W_T) + d*G*(eps_risk + M_cmp + Phi_T + P_Phi)

conditions: bound inside expectation; comparator sequence may be data-dependent

source.label: thm:expected-dynamic
source.quote: ... kappa = sqrt(d) in the oblivious setting and kappa=1 otherwise

tuning: constants c_1, c_2 of Zhang & Cutkosky doubled

source.label: thm:high-prob-static
source.quote: Let PABLO be implemented with [Zhang & Cutkosky, Algorithm 1], and delta in (0,1/3]. Then for any F_0-measurable u in R^d, with probability at least 1-3delta, R_T(u) <= Õ(dG(eps+||u||)log(T/delta)+G||u|| sqrt(dT log(T/delta))).

results.notes: Losses may be adaptive; comparator F_0-measurable. Placed under adaptive-loss setting with that condition.

bound.expression: sqrt(d*(Phi_T + P_Phi)*Min(d*W_T, Omega_T)) + G*sqrt(d*U2_T*log(T/delta)) + d*G*(eps_risk + M_cmp + Phi_T + P_Phi)*log(T/delta)

tuning: parameters chosen depending on G, delta, T, d as in Appendix (c_1, c_2, alpha_1=eps, alpha_2=omega, p_1=2, p_2=log(T+1))

source.label: thm:high-prob-dynamic
source.quote: Let delta in (0,1/4]. Then PABLO applied with Algorithm sub-exponential-dynamic and appropriately-chosen parameters ... guarantees that for any (F_t)-adapted sequence u_{1:T} in R^d, with probability at least 1-4delta it holds that R_T(u_{1:T}) <= Õ(sqrt(d(Phi_T+P_T^Phi)[dV_T ∧ Omega_T]) + G sqrt(d sum ||u_t||^2 log(T/delta)) + dG(eps+M+Phi_T+P_T^Phi) log(T/delta))

results.notes: Appendix gives an explicit constant version. Remark 2 says it extends to arbitrary comparator sequences up to constants.

conditions: losses i.i.d. sub-Gaussian with mean theta and E||l||^2 <= 1
regret measured against the direction theta/||theta|| (direction regret R_T^Z)

source.label: th::lb_unit_ball
source.quote: Assume T>=4d. Then, for any algorithm A playing actions z_1,...,z_T in the unit Euclidean ball it holds that 1. There exists a parameter theta in R^d and a sub-Gaussian distribution P_theta, such that E[l]=theta, E[||l||^2]<=1, for which it holds that R_T^sto(A,theta) := E[R_T^Z(theta/||theta||)] >= sqrt(dT)/64 ∧ T/(12d).

results.notes: Hard instances: theta in {±1/(8 sqrt T)}^d, Gaussian noise N(0, I/(2d)).

source.label: th::lb_unit_ball
source.quote: There exists a sequence of losses l_1,...,l_T satisfying ||l_t||<=1 for all t>=1, a comparator u in B_d, and an absolute constant C such that R_T^Z(u) >= C {sqrt(dT) ∧ T/d} sqrt(d/(d ∨ log(T))).

results.notes: Statement writes R_T^Z(u) without expectation; proof lower-bounds expected regret over learner randomness via randomization over clipped Gaussian losses. Quantity type uncertain.

symbols.n_S: number of step-sizes in the grid S (logarithmic in T)

tuning: alpha = eps/T, gamma = L/T, k=4, grid eta_i = 2^i/(TL) ∧ 1/L

source.label: thm:dynamic-base-olo-tuned
source.quote: For any sequence of L-Lipschitz convex functions f_1,...,f_T and any sequence u_{1:T} in R^d, Algorithm dynamic-meta-olo guarantees R_T(u_{1:T}) <= 4L(|S|eps + M + Phi(||u_T||,T/eps)+P_T^Phi(4T^3/eps)) + 2 sqrt(2(Phi(||u_T||,T/eps)+P_T^Phi(4T^3/eps)) sum ||g_t||^2||u_t||)

results.notes: Deterministic full-information OCO bound (probability field set to expectation for lack of a deterministic option).
